A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E-BATS, and their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are inspectable. However, v2 visibly replaces the token-level loss definition in Equation (3) with 'B.' without providing the full formula elsewhere, limiting comparison of that component.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-recognition experiments, GPU-memory measurements, distribution-shift analyses, and component ablations, including three-seed results in Appendix C.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds sensitivity experiments, prediction-collapse diagnostics, continual-adaptation results, and an emotion-recognition experiment.

M1.justification: Prompt addition, CMA-ES optimization, T-EMA, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. However, the malformed Equation (3) prevents verification of the exact token-level objective. Appendix C.8 reports applying E-BATS to emotion recognition without specifying procedural changes.

E1.justification: Appendix C.8 adds emotion classification on IEMOCAP under Gaussian noise, extending evaluation beyond v1's transcription tasks to a distinct downstream task. The original ASR datasets and acoustic conditions remain.

E2.justification: The same thirteen TTA baselines participate in Tables 1, 2, 6, and 7. The added analyses use existing ablation variants or an unadapted model; TinyTTA is newly cited but is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: The original ASR protocol and default settings remain. Added evaluation designs include parameter grids, candidate and iteration budgets, streams of 100–800 utterances, and prediction-collapse counts. Appendix C.8 additionally evaluates a SpeechBrain emotion model using accuracy under Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.02.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3–C.5 add systematic sensitivity analyses for EMA decay, loss weights, population size, iteration count, and domain complexity; diagnostics of blank and single-character collapse; and adaptation-history experiments. These substantially extend the retained component ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed ablation means and standard deviations in Table 8. The added experiments introduce no additional stated repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: The original Tables 1–8 and memory results are retained. v2 adds sensitivity and stream-length WER results, collapse counts of 990 versus 16 problematic predictions in Table 14, and emotion-recognition accuracy increasing from 38.8% to 43.4% in Appendix C.8. Table 14's WER pair repeats the existing ablation results.

T1.justification: v1's Equation (3) explicitly averages squared differences between source and target token means and standard deviations; v2 replaces this central mathematical definition with 'B.' Conversely, Appendices C.7 and C.9 add CMA-ES complexity arguments and the formal DSUTA/FOA/E-BATS comparison in Table 17. Existing covariate-shift assumptions and FID mathematics remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and concluding summary retain the same novelty, accuracy, and memory-efficiency claims. Section 6 additionally asserts theoretical computational superiority over baselines, referring to the new Appendix C.9.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of tuning stability, optimization saturation, adaptation-history benefits, applicability beyond CTC-based ASR, and theoretical efficiency despite practical latency. Section 5.5 now explicitly recognizes single-character collapse. Some new interpretations overstate their evidence: Appendix C.3.2 calls the default setting best although Table 10 lists 37.7% WER below its 37.9%.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer, identifies clean LibriSpeech as the source of pre-collected statistics, and specifies a 512-dimensional prompt. These are additional disclosures; the original hardware, early-stopping rule, and principal ASR settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to TinyTTA, the original CTC paper, and a wav2vec2 mispronunciation study, supporting discussion of early exits and blank tokens. It also expands the computational comparison with FOA and DSUTA while retaining the original related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence largely remain. Local changes clarify CTC and blank tokens, add appendix cross-references, update affiliation and conference information, and fill the acknowledgments. New appendix subsections surround the retained memory discussion, renumbered from C.3 to C.6.

P2.justification: Tables 9–17 substantially expand the appendix displays with sensitivity grids, collapse diagnostics, stream-length results, and complexity comparisons. The caf-real population sweep is repeated in Tables 11, 12, and 16. Existing Figure 6 is relocated, Table 3 moves above its discussion, and Figures 1–6 otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests, collapse diagnostics, and reproducibility disclosures strengthen empirical support. However, replacing the central loss definition in Equation (3) with 'B.' materially weakens method specification, and some new interpretations conflict with their tables. These substantive benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
